newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African strike has mixed impact at gold mines.
newsitem.headline: S.African strike has mixed impact at gold mines.

text.p: Calls for a one-day general strike to protest against new labour legislation had mixed impact at South African gold mines on Monday morning, mining companies said.
Anglogold, the country's largest producer, said there appeared to be some disruption but large numbers of miners had turned up for work.
"We certainly don't have complete stay-aways. We've got people in significant numbers at work," spokesman James Duncan told Reuters.
Duncan said accurate figures on the level of stay-aways were not yet available.
Anglogold produced 50.2 kg of gold in the three months to March 31, 1997.
Avmin was harder hit. "On the gold mines we've got only essential services working," said spokesman Julian Gwillim.
Gwillim said night shifts at the gold mines, which extract about 100 kg of gold a day, had run as usual.
Gengold said it had operated night and morning shifts as normal.

A spokesman for Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd said the company was still assessing the impact of the strike called by the 1.9 million strong Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) over the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill.
JCI Ltd and Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd officials were not immediately available for comment.
A spokesman for the Chamber of Mines employers group said that based on past experience the one-day general strike was unlikely to have a significant impact on gold production.
